```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tinyAM)
guide_root <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT")
source_files <- if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  c(file.path("R", list.files(file.path(guide_root, "R"), "[.]R$")), "NAMESPACE")
} else {
  list.files(system.file("R", package = "tinyAM"), full.names = TRUE)
}
source_hashes <- tools::md5sum(if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  file.path(guide_root, source_files)
} else source_files)
versions <- c(tinyAM = as.character(packageVersion("tinyAM")),
  R = as.character(getRversion()), RTMB = as.character(packageVersion("RTMB")),
  mgcv = as.character(packageVersion("mgcv")))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  cache.extra = list(versions = versions, sources = unname(source_hashes), inputs = cod_obs))
```

When fish are scarce, a catch or survey sample can record zero for an age
even if fish of that age are present. The default lognormal family uses
positive observations and treats zeros as missing values. Poisson-link delta
(PLD) families use recorded zeros to inform the predicted catch or index.
PLD can be used for catch, survey indices, or both.

## The observation model

Let \(Y_i\) be a recorded catch or survey index for an age and year, and let
\(\widetilde{Y}_i\) be its prediction from the population model. The catch
prediction comes from the Baranov catch equation. The survey prediction is
abundance at sampling time scaled by catchability. Poisson-link delta (PLD)
uses this prediction to explain both the chance of recording a positive
value and the size of positive observations
([Thorson 2018](https://repository.library.noaa.gov/view/noaa/54874), see
also the [sdmTMB Poisson-link delta guide](https://sdmtmb.github.io/sdmTMB/articles/poisson-link.html)).

tinyAM adapts Thorson's parameterization by using the assessment prediction
as the overall mean. Each fleet or survey \(j\) has a soft detection scale
\(\widetilde{Y}_{50,j}\) (the predicted catch or index at which half of
observations are expected to be zero). The prediction and the scale use the
observation's units.

**Encounter.** Conditional on the population states and parameters,
recording a positive value is a binomial outcome with one trial and
probability \(p_{+,i}\). The probability of recording zero is the chance
of zero events under a Poisson distribution with mean \(\lambda_i\).

\[
\lambda_i = \log(2)\frac{\widetilde{Y}_i}{\widetilde{Y}_{50,j}},
\qquad
p_{0,i} = \Pr(Y_i = 0) = e^{-\lambda_i},
\qquad
p_{+,i} = \Pr(Y_i > 0) = 1-p_{0,i}.
\]

Doubling the prediction from the soft detection scale to twice that level
lowers the chance of recording zero from 50% to 25%. The encounter
component uses a complementary log-log link for the probability of a
positive.

\[
\operatorname{cloglog}(p_{+,i})
= \log\!\big[-\log(1-p_{+,i})\big]
= \log\lambda_i.
\]

**Positive observations.** The positive component uses a log link for its
arithmetic mean \(m_{+,i}\), with
\(\log m_{+,i} = \log\widetilde{Y}_i - \log p_{+,i}\).
Dividing by the probability of a positive keeps the average across zeros
and positives equal to the assessment prediction.

\[
m_{+,i} = \frac{\widetilde{Y}_i}{p_{+,i}},
\qquad
p_{+,i}\,m_{+,i} = \widetilde{Y}_i.
\]

The positive distribution can be lognormal, Gamma, or generalized gamma.
For example, with a lognormal positive component,

\[
\log Y_i \mid Y_i > 0
\sim N\!\left(\log m_{+,i}-\frac{\sigma_i^2}{2},\ \sigma_i^2\right).
\]

Here \(\sigma_i\) controls the spread on the log scale. Subtracting
\(\sigma_i^2/2\) gives the positive observations an arithmetic mean of
\(m_{+,i}\). The default, positive-only `lognormal()` family uses the
assessment prediction as its conditional median.
[Observation family reference](../reference/observation_families.html)

**Likelihood.** A recorded zero contributes the log probability of
recording zero. A positive contributes the log probability of recording a
positive plus the log density of its size. Let \(g_{+,i}\) be the chosen
positive density on the log-observation scale.

\[
\ell_i =
\begin{cases}
\log p_{0,i}, & Y_i = 0,\\[4pt]
\log p_{+,i} + \log g_{+,i}(\log Y_i), & Y_i > 0.
\end{cases}
\]

## Apply PLD to Northern cod

```{r zero-counts, include=FALSE}
years <- 1983:2025
ages <- 2:20
zero_count <- function(x) sum(x$obs == 0 & x$year %in% years & x$age %in% ages,
  na.rm = TRUE)
```

Northern cod has **`r zero_count(cod_obs$catch)` recorded catch zeros** and
**`r zero_count(cod_obs$index)` Fall 2J3KL survey zeros** at ages 2–20+ in
1983–2025. This example compares fits using the default lognormal and
the Poisson-link delta lognormal.

```{r fits, cache=TRUE, results="hide"}
ncam <- fit_tam(cod_obs, years = 1983:2025, ages = 2:20,
  N_settings = list(process = "off", init = "exp"),
  rec_settings = list(process = "rw"),
  F_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_form = ~ 1, mean_ages = 5:14),
  M_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_supplied = ~ I(0.3),
    age_breaks = c(2, 5, 8, 21), mean_ages = 5:14),
  catch_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1),
  index_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1, q_form = ~ mono(q_block)),
  silent = TRUE
)

ncam_pld <- update(ncam,
  catch_settings = list(family = pld_lognormal()),
  index_settings = list(family = pld_lognormal()),
  silent = TRUE
)
```

The lognormal fit treats recorded zeros as missing in the likelihood.
Under PLD, a recorded zero contributes the fitted probability of observing
zero. Truly missing observations contribute to neither likelihood. The
lognormal model predicts a median for the positive observations. PLD
predicts an arithmetic mean across zeros and positives.

### Soft detection scales

```{r detection-scales, echo=FALSE}
scales <- subset(tidy_par(ncam_pld)$fixed, par %in% c("y50_catch", "y50_index"))
scales$series <- ifelse(scales$par == "y50_catch", "Commercial catch", "Fall 2J3KL survey")
knitr::kable(scales[c("series", "est", "lwr", "upr", "unit")], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Series", "Soft detection scale", "Lower 95%", "Upper 95%", "Units"))
```

For each series, a fitted mean near its soft detection scale gives a zero
probability near 50%. The table uses the same units as the matrices below.

### Which observations are likely to be zero? {.tabset}

The numbers in the cells are the observations, in thousands of fish. The
colour shows the probability of zero calculated from the fitted mean. Darker
cells have higher probabilities. Grey cells mark missing observations. Hover
over a cell for the full recorded value, fitted mean, and probability. In the
cell labels, `k` means one thousand of the displayed units.

```{r observation-matrices, include=FALSE}
d <- tidy_obs_pred(ncam_pld)
observation_matrix <- function(data) {
  cells <- expand.grid(year = years, age = ages)
  key <- match(paste(cells$year, cells$age), paste(data$year, data$age))
  observed <- data$obs[key]
  predicted <- data$pred_mean[key]
  probability <- ifelse(is.na(observed), NA_real_, data$p_zero[key])
  number <- function(x) format(x, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE, digits = 12)
  rounded <- ifelse(observed < 10, formatC(observed, format = "f", digits = 1),
    ifelse(observed < 10000, as.character(round(observed)),
      paste0(round(observed / 1000), "k")))
  cells$label <- ifelse(is.na(observed), "\u2013",
    ifelse(observed == 0, "0", ifelse(observed < 0.1, "<0.1", rounded)))
  age_labels <- as.character(ages)
  age_labels[length(ages)] <- paste0(max(ages), "+")
  age_label <- age_labels[match(cells$age, ages)]
  fitted_values <- paste0("<br>Fitted mean: ", number(predicted),
    " thousand fish<br>Probability of zero: ", sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * probability))
  hover <- paste0("Year: ", cells$year, "<br>Age: ", age_label, "<br>",
    ifelse(is.na(observed), "Observation: missing",
      paste0("Observed: ", number(observed), " thousand fish", fitted_values)))
  cells$dark <- !is.na(probability) & probability >= 0.65
  color_scale <- list(c(0, "#f8fbfd"), c(0.5, "#aacdde"), c(1, "#244f67"))
  p <- plotly::plot_ly(x = ages, y = years,
    z = matrix(probability, nrow = length(years)),
    text = matrix(hover, nrow = length(years)),
    type = "heatmap", colorscale = color_scale, zmin = 0, zmax = 1,
    xgap = 1, ygap = 1, hoverinfo = "text", hoverongaps = FALSE,
    colorbar = list(title = list(text = "Probability<br>of zero"), tickformat = ".0%"),
    height = 850)
  for (on_dark in c(FALSE, TRUE)) {
    p <- plotly::add_text(p, data = cells[cells$dark == on_dark, ],
      x = ~age, y = ~year, text = ~label, hovertext = hover[cells$dark == on_dark],
      hoverinfo = "text", textposition = "middle center", showlegend = FALSE,
      textfont = list(size = 10, color = if (on_dark) "white" else "#15252d"),
      inherit = FALSE)
  }
  p <- plotly::layout(p, margin = list(t = 70), plot_bgcolor = "#e3e5e8",
    xaxis = list(title = "Age", side = "top", tickvals = ages, ticktext = age_labels,
      showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, automargin = TRUE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Year", range = c(max(years) + .5, min(years) - .5),
      tickvals = c(1983, seq(1985, 2025, by = 5)), showgrid = FALSE))
  htmltools::div(style = "overflow-x: auto;",
    htmltools::div(style = "min-width: 865px;", plotly::config(p, displayModeBar = FALSE)))
}
zero_counts <- lapply(d[c("catch", "index")], tinyAM:::.annual_zero_counts, years = years)
```

The catch recorded `r sum(zero_counts$catch$obs, na.rm = TRUE)` zeros, with
`r round(sum(zero_counts$catch$pred, na.rm = TRUE))` expected under PLD.
The survey recorded `r sum(zero_counts$index$obs, na.rm = TRUE)` zeros, with
`r round(sum(zero_counts$index$pred, na.rm = TRUE))` expected.

#### Catch

```{r catch-matrix, echo=FALSE}
observation_matrix(d$catch)
```

#### Index

```{r index-matrix, echo=FALSE}
observation_matrix(d$index)
```

### How many zeros occur each year? {#annual-zero-counts .tabset}

Dots count the ages with a recorded zero. The line sums the fitted
probabilities of zero over the same sampled ages. Years without observations
leave a gap.

#### Catch {#catch-zero-counts}

```{r catch-zero-counts, echo=FALSE}
tinyAM:::.plot_annual_zeros(zero_counts$catch, height = 320)
```

#### Index {#index-zero-counts}

```{r index-zero-counts, echo=FALSE}
tinyAM:::.plot_annual_zeros(zero_counts$index, height = 320)
```

## Compare the assessments

Only six catches and two survey observations are positive at age 20+.
The 20+ estimates therefore draw heavily on the fitted population dynamics.
The abundance plot shows point estimates on a log scale so differences are
visible when the stock was low. Shading marks the low-stock years from 1992
to 2010.

```{r trajectories, echo=FALSE}
fits <- list(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
terminal <- stack_list(lapply(fits, function(fit) subset(fit$pop$N, age == 20)),
  label = "model")
ssb <- get_ssb(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
terminal_ssb <- subset(ssb, year == max(years))
ssb_change <- with(terminal_ssb,
  sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * (est[model == "PLD"] / est[model == "Lognormal"] - 1)))
low_stock <- list(type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper",
  x0 = 1992, x1 = 2010, y0 = 0, y1 = 1, layer = "below",
  fillcolor = "rgba(170,205,222,0.3)", line = list(width = 0))
plot_trend(terminal, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(2),
  ylab = "Age 20+ abundance (thousands of fish)", add_buttons = FALSE,
  add_intervals = FALSE) |>
  plotly::layout(shapes = list(low_stock),
    yaxis = list(type = "log", range = log10(range(terminal$est) * c(0.8, 1.2))))
plot_trend(ssb, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(2),
  ylab = "Spawning biomass (tonnes)")
```

For 2025 spawning biomass, the change from lognormal to PLD is
`r ssb_change`.

[Northern cod dashboard](../examples/northern-cod-pld/index.html)

## Forecast held-out observations

For each target year from 2006 to 2025, the hindcast fits through the
previous year and forecasts one year with terminal F held constant.
Log-RMSE and MASE compare predicted medians against the same positive
survey observations for both models.
A MASE below one means the model had a lower mean absolute error on the log
scale than a forecast that carried forward the last available positive
observation, evaluated on the same records.

```{r hindcasts, cache=TRUE, dependson="fits"}
hind <- fit_hindcast(ncam, ncam_pld, folds = 20, proj_settings = list(F_mult = 1))
```

The result includes held-out predictions and fold diagnostics. The table
uses only positive survey observations with usable predictions from both
models.

```{r hindcast-scores, echo=FALSE}
survey <- hind$forecast_pairs$index
survey$log_prediction <- ifelse(survey$model == "ncam_pld",
  survey$log_pred_positive, log(survey$pred))
survey <- subset(survey, is.finite(obs) & obs > 0 & is.finite(log_prediction))
key <- with(survey, interaction(fold, year, age, survey, drop = TRUE))
matched <- survey[duplicated(key) | duplicated(key, fromLast = TRUE), ]
labels <- c(ncam = "Lognormal", ncam_pld = "PLD")
scores <- lapply(names(labels), function(model_name) {
  d <- subset(matched, model == model_name)
  data.frame(`Log-RMSE` = compute_hindcast_rmse(d),
    MASE = compute_hindcast_mase(d), check.names = FALSE)
})
scores <- do.call(rbind, scores)
rownames(scores) <- labels
knitr::kable(scores, digits = 2)

brier <- subset(hind$occurrence_scores, model == "ncam_pld" &
  level == "overall" & is.na(horizon))
zero_score <- setNames(sprintf("%.2f", brier$Brier), brier$type)
```

All folds passed numerical checks. PLD reduced both errors on the shared
positive survey observations. Both models had MASE below one.

The hindcast also scores PLD's forecasts of whether each held-out record
was zero. The Brier score averages the squared difference between the
forecast probability of zero and the outcome (1 for a zero and 0 for a
positive). Lower scores are better, with zero indicating perfect
probability forecasts on these records. PLD scored
`r zero_score[["catch"]]` for catch and `r zero_score[["index"]]` for the
survey.

AIC comparisons require a common likelihood for the same observations.
Here the families use different sets of observations because of the zeros.
Conditional AIC is currently available for the all-lognormal fit only.

## References

Thorson, J. T. 2018. Three problems with the conventional delta-model for
biomass sampling data, and a computationally efficient alternative.
*Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences*, 75(9), 1369–1382.
[doi:10.1139/cjfas-2017-0266](https://doi.org/10.1139/cjfas-2017-0266).

```{r dashboard-export, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
if (nzchar(dashboard_cache)) {
  if (!nzchar(guide_root)) stop("Set TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT to the checkout when exporting guide fits.")

    sources = setNames(unname(source_hashes), source_files),
    background = paste(
      "### Northern cod observation families",
      "These NCAM-inspired fits use 1983–2025 and ages 2–20+. The lognormal fit uses positive observations. The PLD fit also uses recorded zeros in both catch and the Fall 2J3KL survey.",
      "See the [Poisson-link delta guide](../../articles/poisson-link-delta.html) for the equations and fitted soft detection scales.",
      sep = "\n\n")), dashboard_cache)
}
```
